meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Luxembourg (unitary national jurisdiction; no sub-state tax distinction)

applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Luxembourg–China Double Taxation Agreement (1994, as amended by subsequent protocols)
Belgo-Luxembourg Economic Union (BLEU)–China Bilateral Investment Treaty (signed 14 November 2005, replacing the 1984 China–BLEU BIT)
Luxembourg–United States Income Tax Treaty (signed 3 April 1996, as amended by the 2009 protocol)
OECD Multilateral Convention to Implement Tax Treaty Related Measures (MLI) covering Luxembourg's tax treaties
EU Treaties and the EEA establishment and capital freedoms (intra-EU direct investment protection)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (most recently implementing EU Directive 2018/843); Law of 13 July 2017 on the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE), as amended; Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended; Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS); CSSF Regulation 12-02 as amended (for AML/CFT professional standards applicable to supervised professionals)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified true copy of the passport of each incorporator, manager (gérant) and ultimate beneficial owner
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: National passport authority of the country of origin, certified by a local notary or commissioner and apostilled by the Ministry of Foreign Affairs of that country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization (Hague Apostille for 1961 Hague Convention states; Luxembourg Embassy consular legalization for all other states)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Police certificate / certificate of good conduct (criminal record extract equivalent to bulletin n° 2) for each natural-person manager and for each UBO acting as director or authorised signatory
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Ministry of Justice or national criminal records bureau of the country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization (official sworn translation into French or English required)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of registration and good standing of any corporate shareholder, together with the corporate resolution authorizing subscription of SARL shares and designation of the manager
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country companies registry or competent registrar and corporate secretary of the shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization (official sworn translation into French or English required)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank certificate of an account opened or blocked in Luxembourg (or a sworn bank reference letter from the subscriber's home-country bank) evidencing the minimum share capital of EUR 12,000 and its source of funds
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Luxembourg credit institution or the subscriber's home-country bank
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille OR Consular Legalization (if signed abroad, with apostille or consular authentication and sworn translation)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory pre-signing screening of all incorporators, managers, shareholders, beneficial owners and signatories against the OFAC SDN List, the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List (implemented in Luxembourg by Grand-Ducal regulations and national provisions), the UN Security Council consolidated sanctions lists (Resolutions 1267/1988, 2231 and successor regimes), and the Luxembourg national list administered by the Cellule de Renseignement Financier (CRF); PEP status is determined under Article 3 of the Law of 12 November 2004 as amended, applying enhanced due diligence for politically exposed persons, their family members and close associates; responsibility for the screening rests jointly on the Luxembourg notary and the engaged AML compliance officer, with screening evidence refreshed within 90 days before the notarial act and retained for at least five years after the business relationship ends; any unverified beneficial owner or inconsistent source-of-funds answer must be resolved before execution or, failing that, be reported by the notary to the CRF as a suspicious transaction.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) operated by Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — official electronic portal www.lbr.lu (including the RESA electronic gazette for statutory publications)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: The company name must be written in Latin-alphabet script, must not conflict with any existing RCS denomination, and must not be contrary to public order or misleading within the meaning of Article 1-2 of the Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies; French is the standard registry filing language, while German and English names are accepted; non-Latin script names must be transliterated into Latin script and accompanied by an officially sworn translation; the distinguishing element must be followed by the legal-form identifier 'Société à Responsabilité Limitée' or the abbreviation 'SARL'.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: LUXEMBOURG (as a distinctive element causing territorial or official patronage confusion)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the RCS/LBR registrar refuses the proposed name, the incorporating notary lodges a written reconsideration request with the Registrar within 15 days of the refusal notice, annexing a corrected alternative denomination or evidence of prior trademark rights and actual use; if the reconsideration is refused, the applicant may initiate a voluntary-jurisdiction appeal before the Tribunal d'arrondissement de Luxembourg (chambre commerciale) within two months of the final refusal, and a further appeal lies with the Cour d'appel; until the dispute is finally resolved, the registry will suspend the name reservation and may, upon a notary's application, extend the initial 30-day window until the judicial decision becomes final.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not acceptable as the sole seat. A Luxembourg SARL must possess a real registered office and central administration in Luxembourg (Article 2-1 and related provisions of the Law of 10 August 1915); the freeze-dried pet-food manufacturing business additionally requires a physical production and storage establishment that is registered and approved by the Administration luxembourgeoise vétérinaire et alimentaire (ALVA) under EU Regulation (EC) No 1069/2009 and Regulation (EC) No 183/2005 on feed hygiene. A virtual office may only be used as an auxiliary correspondence and billing address alongside the substantive operational facility.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: High: 85%–95% probability of at least one unannounced physical on-site inspection by the ALVA veterinary and official-food-control authorities, municipal inspectors, or the Ministry of Middle Classes during the first 12 months of operations, because the establishment processes animal-derived raw materials intended for pet consumption, which is a priority segment of official control plans under EU Regulation (EU) 2017/625.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Regulated notarial tariff and customary practice: flat-band fee of EUR 1,200–2,500 for a standard SARL incorporation act

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name availability search and name reservation at the RCS
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory RCS fee schedule (EUR 60–80 per search or reservation request)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: RCS registration of the company and filing of the incorporation dossier (including the register extract of the SARL)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory inscription fee of the RCS and electronic file processing fee (EUR 100–170)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Publication of the incorporation deed in the Recueil électronique des sociétés et associations (RESA)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: ALVA establishment registration and prior approval for animal by-product processing (freeze-dried pet food)
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official-control and establishment-registration fee schedule under EU Regulation (EU) 2017/625 and national food-chain fee provisions

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille and consular legalization of foreign passports, criminal-record extracts, corporate resolutions, and bank reference letters

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Registered translator per-page tariff (approximately EUR 25–40 per page)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (as consolidated and amended by the Law of 23 June 2016), Articles 710-1 to 710-22 governing the Société à Responsabilité Limitée (SARL); Law of 19 December 2002 on the Register of Commerce and Companies (RCS).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of Association (Acte Constitutionnel / Statuts) executed by authentic notarial deed before a Luxembourg notary public
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum subscribed capital EUR 12,000 (approx. USD 13,000); the capital must be fully subscribed; at least 10% (EUR 1,200) of each share's nominal value must be paid up in cash on a bank account opened in the company's name before notarization; no statutory escrow account requirement applies to the SARL form.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED: that the incorporation of the Société à Responsabilité Limitée be and is hereby approved; that the initial share capital of EUR 12,000 be subscribed in full by the founding shareholders; that the registered office be established at [registered address], Luxembourg; that the Articles of Association as notarized be adopted in full; that [Name] be and is hereby appointed as sole Manager (Gérant) empowered with full management authority; that the Manager be authorized to open bank accounts, to file the incorporation dossier with the Luxembourg Business Registers and the RCS, to complete all tax, environmental, veterinary, and establishment registrations, and to take every act necessary for the lawful commencement of freeze-dried pet food manufacture.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Notarization of the Articles of Association and Capital Deposit Verification
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary public (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the French-language Articles of Association (statuts) containing all mandatory SARL clauses (corporate name, registered office, purpose, capital, share allocation, management powers, duration, liquidation). The founding shareholders must pre-fund the company's blocked bank account with the minimum paid-up portion (EUR 1,200). The notary verifies identity, capital contribution, and legality of clauses, then reads, authenticates, and signs the deed electronically, transmitting the dossier to the RCS.
required_dossiers: Draft Articles of Association (statuts) in French
Notarized identification documents (passport or national ID) of all founders
Bank certificate evidencing deposit of paid-up capital (minimum EUR 1,200)
Lease agreement or letter of comfort for the registered office address
Declaration of non-disqualification (absence of bankruptcy/conviction) for the Manager
Anti-money-laundering declarations and source-of-funds documentation for each shareholder
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary issues a query on legal form or capital proof, remedy deficiencies (amend clauses, supplement the capital deposit, or provide clean AML documentation) and re-execute the deed within 15 days; if founders are non-resident, obtain apostilled/legalized corporate authorizations from the home jurisdiction before re-notarization.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Registration with the Luxembourg Business Registers (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary submits the incorporation dossier electronically to the RCS. The registry performs the legal review of the deed, verifies the proposed company name against conflicts, confirms the manager appointment, and issues the RCS registration number. The company acquires legal personality on the date of registration.
required_dossiers: Authentic notarial deed of incorporation
Coordinating file (Form C) completed on the RCS e-portal
Power of attorney if filing through counsel
Passport copies of shareholders and the Manager
Written acceptance of appointment signed by the Manager
Registered office consent (lease title) and domiciliation agreement
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS issues a regularization request (e.g., name conflict or missing consent), submit corrected exhibits within the statutory deadline (generally 15 days); re-file the coordinating form via the RCS e-portal; if registration is refused, apply for a rectification order from the competent district court of Luxembourg.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication in the Official Electronic Gazette (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After RCS registration, the notary's deed extract and the RCS filing particulars are transmitted automatically for publication in the RESA. Publication is mandatory and confers opposability of the statutes and registered particulars against third parties. The company's legal existence is publicly evidenced by the RCS extract and RESA publication reference.
required_dossiers: RCS registration extract
Notarized deed of incorporation
Confirmation slip of electronic RESA transfer from the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is delayed or contains inaccuracies, request correction from the RCS within 8 days of the defective publication; re-submit the corrected extract to the RESA to restore accurate third-party notice.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministry of the Economy — Direction Générale des Classes Moyennes via the Guichet.lu e-portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the establishment authorization application electronically on Guichet.lu before commencing any commercial activity. The applicant must demonstrate the Manager's good character (no disqualifying criminal or bankruptcy records) and, because the activity is food/feed production, present recognized professional qualifications or prove the engagement of a qualified technical supervisor. The authorization is personal, non-transferable, and must be maintained for the life of the company.
required_dossiers: Guichet.lu application form (autorisation d'établissement)
Judicial record (extrait du casier judiciaire) of the Manager
Evidence of professional qualification (diploma or vocational certificate in food/feed technology) or appointment of a qualified deputy
RCS registration extract and Articles of Association
Lease agreement and floor plan of the production facility
Statement of adequate third-party liability and professional insurance
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If refused, file a hierarchical appeal (recours gracieux) with the Minister of the Economy within 3 months, supplementing the file with missing qualification evidence or appointing a qualified Manager; in final resort, appeal to the Administrative Tribunal of Luxembourg within 3 months of refusal.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: VAT, Social Security, and Customs Registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT); Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS); Administration des Douanes et Accises
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the Luxembourg VAT registration via the AEDT (Form 640) to obtain a TVA identification number; register the employer with the CCSS for mandatory sickness and pension coverage of employees; apply for an EORI number from the Customs Administration to enable EU import/export of raw material and finished pet food; complete the UBO register filing with the RCS if not already done by the notary.
required_dossiers: VAT Form 640 (with necessary annexes)
RCS extract and notarized Articles of Association
Identity documents of the Manager and beneficial owners
Bank account confirmation (RIB) in the company's name
Lease or ownership title for the production premises
Employment declarations for the initial payroll (formerly sworn declarations)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If registrations are delayed, issue formal reminders to the AEDT and CCSS, correct any identification mismatches, and file late or provisional returns to avoid periodic penalties; if the UBO filing is incomplete, submit corrective filings via the LBR portal; obtain ex-officio VAT registration under Article 10 of the Luxembourg VAT law if the administration fails to respond within the statutory period.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministry of Agriculture, Viticulture and Rural Development — Veterinary Services Administration (Administration des Services Vétérinaires, ASV)
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Establishment Approval for Pet Food and Animal Feed Production (Agrément d'Établissement) under Article 10 of EU Regulation (EC) No. 183/2005 on feed hygiene and EU Regulation (EC) No. 1069/2009 on animal by-products

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'Environnement (Environmental Administration of the Grand Duchy of Luxembourg)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Class 2 environmental authorization (autorisation de classe 2) required for the operation of the freeze-drying pet food plant; a simplified declaration may only apply below the low-capacity threshold of the grand-ducal implementing regulations; a full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) dossier may be required if the facility's treatment capacity exceeds 300 tonnes per day of raw animal material, subject to case-by-case screening (notice to that effect from the Administration de l'Environnement).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Industrial wastewater discharges must comply with the grand-ducal regulation of 11 October 2010 on discharge limits for industrial effluents; VOC emissions must respect the levels prescribed by Directive 2010/75/EU (Industrial Emissions Directive) and the associated national implementation thresholds; freeze-drying condensate, adhered fat, and Category 3 animal-by-product waste must be rendered and disposed of through an approved facility under EU Regulation 1069/2009 with full lot traceability; odor emissions are checked against the ASV and environmental administration neighborhood nuisance standards with mandatory mitigation (biofilters or thermal oxidizers).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Fire safety certification issued by the Corps Grand-Ducal d'Incendie et de Secours (CGDIS) covering the production hall, ammonia refrigeration enclosure, and warehouse; structural load inspection certificate from an approved state-appointed engineer validating the vacuum freeze-drying chambers and structural floor load; workplace occupational health clearance delivered by the Inspection du Travail et des Mines (ITM) covering confined-space entry permits, ammonia leak detection protocols, manual lifting limits, and personal protective equipment standards; municipal building permit (permis de construire) confirming zoning conformity for industrial pet food manufacturing at the designated address in Luxembourg.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) for VAT matters; Administration des contributions directes (ACD) for direct tax matters; Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) for entity registration. Official portals: guichet.lu, MyGuichet.lu, eTVA.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A Luxembourg SARL receives a 13-digit business registration number (numéro de matricule d'identité) upon RCS filing. The VAT identification number (numéro d'identification à la TVA) is issued automatically by the AEDT after RCS registration for resident entities. Foreign entities without a permanent establishment in Luxembourg must submit a non-established taxable person registration form to the AEDT, attaching the foreign business registration certificate, constitutional documents, identification of the Luxembourg fiscal agent (if required), and, where applicable, the EU VAT number and a declaration of planned activities. Approval may take 1 to 4 weeks; an ACD declaration may also be required if the activity creates a Luxembourg permanent establishment.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (resident SARL subject to corporate income tax, municipal business tax, and net wealth tax on worldwide income; no pass-through treatment)
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not operate a check-the-box regime. Available statutory elections include: (i) VAT group election under Article 60 of the Luxembourg VAT Law for financially, economically and organically linked entities; (ii) corporate tax consolidation (régime d'intégration fiscale) for resident parent companies holding at least 95% of a qualifying subsidiary for at least five years; (iii) the simplified flat-rate VAT exemption scheme for small businesses within the domestic threshold; (iv) limited hybrid mismatch adjustments under ATAD navigation, including opting into the UE provisions and defensive rule elections via bilateral treaty relief; (v) joint taxation of spouses for personal income tax, inapplicable to SARL.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT (Taxe sur la Valeur Ajoutée - TVA)
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: EUR 35,000 annual taxable turnover for the small-business VAT exemption for domestic established taxable persons; EUR 0 for non-established suppliers making taxable supplies in Luxembourg; EUR 10,000 EU-wide OSS threshold for intra-Community distance sales of goods and cross-border digital services
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: No mandatory real-time continuous transaction controls (CTC) or digital stamping is currently in force. B2B electronic invoicing is optional but accepted. Invoices to Luxembourg public-sector entities must be submitted electronically via the Peppol BIS 3.0 network or an equivalent public procurement e-invoicing portal. All VAT-registered businesses must file periodic VAT returns electronically via eTVA and retain underlying records for ten years. The AEDT may require SAF-T or structured data files during audit for cross-checking; no real-time clearance is imposed.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating applies to supplies of finished freeze-dried pet treats and raw-meat kibble physically exported from Luxembourg to a destination outside the European Union, provided the goods leave the EU by the end of the month following the supply and are supported by transport/customs evidence. Intra-EU supplies to taxable customers may be zero-rated when the customer communicates a valid EU VAT identification number and the goods are dispatched to another Member State. Ancillary freight and insurance services may be zero-rated if directly related to an export supply. Packaging and processing services performed on goods destined for export may also qualify under the merchanting and tolling provisions if properly evidenced.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (EX-A / common transit declaration T1) validated by Luxembourg Customs with the assigned MRN
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or CMR transport document evidencing physical dispatch from Luxembourg and arrival outside the European Union
Commercial invoice and packing list consistent with the customs declaration and VAT invoice
Purchase order or distribution contract with the foreign buyer showing Incoterms 2020 (FCA, CPT, or CIP) and the place of delivery
Inward Remittance Certificate or bank receipt confirming payment from the foreign customer within the contractual and statutory periods
Delivery confirmation signed by the foreign importer or customs release documentation evidencing arrival in the destination country
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: The AEDT may conduct documentation audits and physical tracing of exported goods. If zero-rating is claimed without genuine customs clearance, transport evidence, or payment repatriation, the VAT becomes immediately due and is clawed back with delay interest at 0.6% per month (or such statutory rate from time to time applicable) plus administrative fines of up to EUR 25,000. Fraudulent documentation or intentionally false customs declarations may trigger criminal prosecution and imprisonment. Repayment of temporally claimed VAT may also be reversed if the exporter cannot demonstrate the goods left the EU within the statutory deadline. Retrospective adjustment periods vary from three years generally to ten years for intended fraud.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL). Luxembourg does not maintain a separate foreign-exchange administration; exchange-control and payment-system oversight is shared between the BCL, the Luxembourg Ministry of Finance, and the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF) for banking and AML supervision. The BCL is the Eurosystem central bank, operator of TARGET2-T2 participation, and national compiler of balance-of-payments statistics.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Luxembourg has full capital-account and current-account convertibility under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union and the general EU legal framework for cross-border payments. There are no exchange-control approvals, no mandatory conversion obligation, and no regulatory barrier to profit repatriation for a resident SARL. Dividends and shareholder-loan repayments may be paid abroad provided the corporate-law solvency tests under the Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies are met. The main frictions are AML/KYC source-of-funds verification, balance-of-payments statistical reporting thresholds administered by the BCL, and the Luxembourg 15% domestic dividend withholding tax, which is generally reduced to 0% under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive for a qualifying EU corporate shareholder holding at least 10% of the SARL share capital for an uninterrupted two-year period.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None applicable. Luxembourg imposes no statutory timeline for repatriation, no minimum retention in Luxembourg, and no mandatory conversion ratio for export receipts. Export proceeds in USD, GBP, CNY, or other freely convertible currencies may be retained indefinitely in a Luxembourg foreign-currency account or converted into EUR at the prevailing commercial bank exchange rate. The only related obligations are the SARL's record-keeping duty, standard SWIFT reference/purpose information, BCL balance-of-payments reporting where the transaction exceeds statistical thresholds, and EU cash-control declarations for physical movement of currency above EUR 10,000.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque et Caisse d'Épargne de l'État, Luxembourg (BCEE / Spuerkeess)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account (blocked account for SARL-in-formation) and Operational Payments Account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: Banque Internationale à Luxembourg, société anonyme (BIL)
tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Capital Escrow Account and Operational Payments Account with multi-currency capability
Capital Escrow Account and Operational Payments Account with trade-finance desk
Operational Payments Account and Documentary/Commercial Letter of Credit facilities
Operational Payments Account; viable for day-to-day treasury but less specialised in blocked capital accounts

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Moderate but strictly limited. A Luxembourg or other EEA-authorised e-money institution (EMI) may provide payment accounts, SEPA and SWIFT-style transfers, issuer/payment acquiring services, and FX conversion under the EU Payment Services Directive (PSD2) and the CSSF e-money framework. An EMI is not a credit institution: it cannot accept deposits, issue a blocked capital-escrow certificate, grant credit, or provide the full treasury security of a BCL-licensed bank. A non-EEA digital EMI should be treated as high-risk and unsuitable for principal SARL treasury operations because of weaker supervisory reach, absence of deposit protection, and potential restriction by Luxembourg banks on receiving funds from unregulated or thin-capitalised payment firms. For the Freeze-Dried Pet Raw Meat project, an EMI may be used only as a secondary collection/payout rail for Platform_Pay and small e-commerce sales, while the primary operational and escrow accounts must remain with a Luxembourg credit institution.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical attendance of at least one managing director or a duly authorised officer is generally required or commercially expected during account opening. Luxembourg AML law does not impose an absolute statutory requirement of face-to-face interview if the bank can perform reliable remote/electronic identification through a certified video-identification process, a qualified electronic signature, or a recognised eIDAS-based onboarding system. In practice, BCL-supervised banks usually require a video call or in-person visit for final compliance approval; passports, proof of residence, register of beneficiaries, source-of-wealth justifications, and corporate constitutional documents of all shareholders must be provided. A non-EU corporate shareholder may additionally require apostilled and translated corporate documents.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Undisclosed or complex ultimate beneficial ownership chain, especially through a non-EU company with weak AML regulation.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Company group chart; RCS Luxembourg excerpt for the SARL and corresponding registered-office excerpts for all foreign shareholders; articles of association and memorandum; register of shareholders; UBO register declaration; certified passport copies and proof of address for every natural-person UBO; notarised corporate resolutions approving the incorporation and capital contribution; source-of-funds statement explaining the commercial origin of each capital payment; professional bank references; apostilles and certified translations.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Cross-border trade payments to raw-meat suppliers in jurisdictions categorised by the bank as high-risk or subject to enhanced due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Validated supplier due-diligence questionnaires; executed supply contracts; commercial invoices and packing lists; EU TRACES import notifications; veterinary health certificates and sanitary certificates required for animal-origin pet-food inputs; import licences and customs declarations; shipping documents such as bills of lading; product specifications and HACCP/FSSC 22000 certification; explanation of the commercial purpose and projected payment flows for each supplier country.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Platform_Pay and e-commerce settlement flows that appear fragmented, with third-party payout accounts or unclear merchant-of-record structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Executed merchant agreements with the payment platform; payout schedule and bank-statement reconciliation; order-level transaction reporting; platform settlement API reports; customer refund and dispute policy; product liability and recall insurance certificates; clear organisational chart showing the SARL as legal merchant of record; consolidated monthly sales reports matched to inward SWIFT or platform payouts.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Misclassification of the freeze-dried pet-food business as a high-risk food-processing activity requiring special veterinary/food-safety licences.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Registration or approval of the processing premises with the Luxembourg competent authority under Regulation (EC) No 1069/2009 on animal by-products; veterinary establishment approval certificate; HACCP plan; ISO 22000 or FSSC 22000 certificates; raw-material traceability records; product risk assessment for raw freeze-dried pet treats; legal opinion confirming product classification for customs and veterinary purposes; affidavits from company directors describing the actual manufacturing process.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: The inbound equity injection for the LU_SARL must be routed by SWIFT MT103 or equivalent high-value transfer from the foreign shareholder to a blocked capital-escrow account opened in the name of the SARL-in-formation with a Luxembourg credit institution or the BCL. The payment reference must state clearly: 'Equity capital contribution to LU_SARL [name] under Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915'. The Luxembourg bank will verify receipt of funds and, after notarisation of the incorporation deed, release the blocked funds to the company's operational account. For later capital increases, the same blocked-account procedure applies and the BCL balance-of-payments statistical classification should be 'Direct Investment – Equity Capital'. The inbound transfer narrative should include the legal entity identifiers of both remitter and beneficiary, the ultimate beneficial owner screen, and the source-of-funds documentation. Foreign-currency inbound amounts may be converted to EUR at the receiving bank's market rate; no exchange-control permit is required.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements should use SWIFT MT103 for non-urgent supplier payments and documentary clearing, MT700 for issuance of a Commercial Letter of Credit and MT707 for amendments when procuring bulk raw meat or animal-derived ingredients from third countries. Within the euro area, SEPA Credit Transfers are acceptable for low-value EU supplier payments. For Platform_Pay e-commerce operations, daily or periodic settlement payouts should be redirected from the payment platform to the SARL's Luxembourg operational account, with reconciliation files retained for audit. All disbursements must identify the underlying commercial invoice, Incoterms 2020 rule, HS classification of freeze-dried pet food and raw pet-food inputs, and be backed by EU veterinary import documentation. A single BCL-supervised bank should act as the clear treasury hub to reduce counterparty clearance failures and ensure liquidity forecasting.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable FX forward contracts with a Luxembourg credit institution or EU/EEA investment firm, documented under an ISDA or EVS master agreement, used to fix the EUR cost of confirmed USD/GBP/CNY raw-material payables for up to twelve months.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) for emerging-market currencies where a deliverable interbank forward is unavailable in Luxembourg; settlement is made in EUR, must be supported by documented underlying trade exposure, and is subject to ISDA margin provisions where the counterparty is a financial entity.

Cross-currency swaps for long-term shareholder loans or intercompany treasury balances, permitting conversion of fixed-rate foreign-currency liability into EUR floating or fixed interest streams, with credit support annexed and EMIR clearing thresholds assessed for each counterparty.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholders' general meeting approving the annual accounts
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders' general meeting (corporate act recorded in the statutory minute book)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 6 months after the close of the financial year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Irregular approval or failure to hold the meeting at the required time may render the financial statements not properly approved; directors incur civil liability for delay or non-compliance

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of annual accounts with the Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers / Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (LBR/RCS)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after approval by the shareholders' meeting and no later than 7 months after financial year-end
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Court order may compel filing, administrative fines may be imposed for late deposit, and repeated non-compliance may result in judicial strike-off or winding-up of the SARL

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax and municipal business tax annual return
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration des contributions directes (ACD), bureau d'imposition des collectivités
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a calendar-year SARL, filing generally due by 31 December of the year following the tax year; extensions are subject to ACD approval
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Risk of default tax assessment, late-filing surcharges, late-payment interest on unpaid corporate and municipal business taxes, and financial penalties

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Filed together with or alongside the corporate income tax return for the relevant tax year
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default assessment, monthly late-payment interest, and administrative penalties for late or incorrect filing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Luxembourg VAT annual recapitulative and administrative return, where applicable
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AED)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally due by 31 March following the calendar year unless the taxpayer is on monthly or quarterly VAT filing obligations
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fines, late-payment interest, and in cases of deliberate omission, criminal VAT penalties

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual confirmation of the beneficial owner statement in the Luxembourg RBE register
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registre des bénéficiaires effectifs (RBE), operated by the Luxembourg Business Registers
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual confirmation on the RBE portal; any shareholding transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be declared within 1 month of the event
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Administrative fines and potential criminal sanctions for false, late, or incomplete declarations; continued non-compliance may trigger register rectification procedures and enhanced AML/KYC scrutiny

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A SARL is subject to mandatory independent audit if it exceeds at least two of the following criteria on two consecutive balance sheet dates: total balance sheet EUR 4,400,000; net turnover EUR 8,800,000; average number of employees 50.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Luxembourg legal accounting framework based on the Loi du 19 décembre 2002 and the Luxembourg plan comptable; IFRS is used where required for consolidated accounts but is not mandatory for the individual annual accounts of a SARL.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: The SARL must maintain an accurate beneficial owner register. Any shareholding transfer or change in beneficial ownership must be filed with the RBE within 1 month. The RBE portal requires an annual confirmation that the beneficial owner statement remains correct, and share transfers become effective against the company only after entry in the statutory register of members.

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 1,800–4,500 per annum for Luxembourg registered office, domiciliation, and corporate secretarial agent services
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 10,000–30,000 per annum for a statutory audit when the SARL exceeds the applicable Luxembourg audit thresholds

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Luxembourg corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) is levied at a headline rate of 17% (15% for taxable income up to EUR 175,000 for the 2024 tax year; 17% above). The effective aggregate CIT rate in Luxembourg City, including the 7% unemployment fund surcharge and municipal business tax (taxe d'exploitation communale) at the standard 6.75% rate, is 24.94%. A SARS (solidarity surcharge) of 7% applies to CIT, capped at 17% base rate effectively. The Intellectual Property (IP) box regime provides an 80% exemption on qualifying IP-derived income, resulting in an 80% deductible exemption and effective rate of approximately 5% on such income. The commercial activity of vacuum freeze-drying manufacture of pet treats is not eligible for the IP box. Additional incentives include the investment tax credit (crédit d'impôt pour investissements) for eligible tangible assets and the 30% participation exemption for capital gains on qualifying share disposals, which does not apply to trading income. No statutory tax holiday applies to the freeze-dried pet food manufacturing sector. A 15% minimum CIT base applies to certain excessive interest and royalty payments under the anti-abuse rules.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Corporate income tax return form 540 (Déclaration de l'impôt sur le revenu des collectivités) submitted via the Luxembourg direct tax electronic portal MyGuichet.lu (eTVA/CIT filing module), with mandatory attachment of financial statements and supporting schedules. Municipal business tax declaration is integrated within the combined Form 540/1100 filing package.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual (tax year aligned with the fiscal year; filing due no later than 31 December of the year following the calendar year in which the fiscal year ends, unless an extension is granted).
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: For a Luxembourg SARL with a fiscal year ending 31 December, the corporate tax return must be filed by 31 December of the subsequent year. A six-month extension is available upon written application to the Direct Tax Administration (Administration des contributions directes, ACD). The assessment (rôle) is issued after filing and payment of the estimated tax instalments.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 404/406 – Identification Section (RCS and tax file number)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal entity identification: Luxembourg trade and companies register number (RCS), Luxembourg income tax file number (matricule d'impôt), registered address, legal form code, and director identification details.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a SARL established in Luxembourg, all shareholders may be non-residents; the full legal name, residential or corporate address, country of tax residence, and Luxembourg tax identification number of each director/managing director must be disclosed. Non-resident tax identification numbers are recorded but not used for rate determination; they are cross-checked for beneficial ownership declaration under the register of beneficial owners (RBE).

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Declaration of gross business income including sales revenue from wholesale and retail sale of vacuum freeze-dried raw meat pet products, movement in inventories of finished goods and work-in-progress, and other operating income, excluding exempt participation dividends.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All revenue booked in Luxembourg SARL accounts must be declared irrespective of non-resident shareholder residence. Export sales to EU Member States and third-countries, including sales executed through platform payment rails, are declared as Luxembourg-source commercial income under the full-liability principle.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Business expenses deductible in computing taxable profit: raw material purchases of freeze-dried meat, direct production costs, packaging, utilities, rent, personnel wages, marketing, shipping and fulfilment charges, platform payment processing fees, depreciation of specialized freeze-drying equipment, and administrative overheads. Non-deductible items (fines, certain representation expenses) are added back.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Expenses paid to non-resident affiliated entities are deductible subject to transfer pricing arm's length documentation and, for cross-border payments exceeding EUR 250,000 per category, the filing of Form 740 (intragroup transactions report). Payments routed through platform payment settlement wallets must be substantiated by contracts and receipts.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Interest income, dividends, exchange gains/losses, and deductible interest expenses under the interest limitation rule (30% EBITDA cap or EUR 3 million threshold, whichever higher).
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Interest paid to non-resident related parties is deductible only subject to ATAD interest limitation rules and substance requirements; beneficial ownership and DTA entitlement must be evidenced for any reduced withholding rate.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim of prior-year tax losses available for offset against current-year taxable income, subject to the 17-year carry-forward period for losses incurred until FY 2017 and the five-year carryforward period for losses incurred after 1 January 2017.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss offset claims do not require non-resident shareholder action. In an ownership change exceeding 25% (direct or indirect), the loss carryforward is proportionately denied under the change-in-control anti-loss-trading provision, unless a commercial justification is demonstrated to the ACD.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Global minimum tax (Pillar Two) forms, IP box deduction, investment tax credit claims, and foreign tax credit claims for profits taxed abroad.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Luxembourg SARL owned by non-residents is subject to global minimum tax top-up obligations only if the consolidated group revenue exceeds EUR 750 million; for a typical standalone freeze-dried pet food manufacturer below that threshold, no top-up applies. Non-resident shareholders cannot claim the investment tax credit.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Mandatory annual report of intragroup transactions with related non-resident and resident entities: nature, volume, pricing method, and financial data for controlled transactions exceeding EUR 250,000 in sales, purchases, interest, royalties, or management fees.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A Luxembourg SARL engaged in freeze-dried pet food manufacturing that transacts with non-resident founders, raw materials suppliers, or IP licensors must file the Annex to Form 740, disclosing the applied transfer pricing method, comparable data, and the arm's length range.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the corporate tax return triggers an automatic penalty of EUR 250 (minimum) plus EUR 100 per month of delay up to EUR 2,000. Inaccuracy caused by wilful omission triggers a surcharge of 10% of the deficient tax. If no return is filed, the ACD may issue assessments based on its own estimation, with late payment interest of 0.6% per month on unpaid CIT and municipal business tax. Misdeclaration intended to evade taxation may result in the application of an intentional error penalty of up to 50% of evaded tax (Article 134bis LIR).

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 15% statutory Luxembourg dividend withholding tax on cash and in-kind distributions from a Luxembourg SARL to shareholders, applicable regardless of shareholder residence.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: Treaty relief for dividend, interest, and royalty payments is applied administratively in Luxembourg through a two-tier protocol. First, at source, the Luxembourg SARL may apply the reduced treaty rate or exemption only where the beneficial owner (shareholder) has provided a valid Luxembourg tax residence certificate for the relevant calendar year plus a shareholder self-certification confirming treaty entitlement and beneficial ownership. The Luxembourg withholding agent (the SARL) must keep the documentation in its files before the payment date. Second, if the full 15% statutory withholding tax has been deducted, a non-resident shareholder can file a refund claim with the Luxembourg Direct Tax Administration within the statute of limitations (five years) using Form 402, attaching the tax residence certificate (TRC) issued by the shareholder's country of residence, audited financial statements, and evidence of beneficial ownership. For EU parent companies, the Parent-Subsidiary Directive (2011/96/EU) provides a 0% withholding tax on dividends provided the shareholder holds at least 10% of the distributing SARL's capital or share voting rights for an uninterrupted period of at least 12 months and is resident in an EU/EEA Member State. A Luxembourg SARL must still verify anti-abuse substance conditions and the beneficial ownership requirement before granting exemption.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Statutory rates: 15% withholding tax on Luxembourg-source royalties (including licence fees for patents, trade marks, know-how, software and similar intangibles) and 15% on interest (with limited statutory exemptions). No withholding tax on interest paid to EU/EEA resident companies on qualifying corporate debt, subject to the Interest and Royalty Directive (2003/49/EC), provided a 10% shareholding or EUR 100,000 minimum holding for at least one year, and to anti-abuse residence and substance conditions. Treaty rates for royalties generally range from 0% to 10%; the Luxembourg–United States DTA provides a 0% royalty rate, Luxembourg–China DTA provides 6%, Luxembourg–Japan DTA provides 0% or 10% depending on IP type. Treaty interest rates typically 0% to 10%. Application of a reduced treaty rate follows the same TRC plus beneficial ownership certification protocol. For royalties paid to non-residents, the interest and royalty directive exemption is unavailable unless the recipient is a qualifying EU affiliate.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Luxembourg applies an objective threshold requiring a Luxembourg resident entity (including SARL) to prepare and file with its corporate income tax return a transfer pricing documentation report (Annex 740) for intragroup transactions exceeding EUR 250,000 in aggregate per transaction category in a tax year. There is no separate local file/master file threshold under domestic law; however, for entities belonging to an MNE group with a consolidated turnover above EUR 750 million, Luxembourg implements the OECD Country-by-Country (CbC) reporting requirement, together with mandatory Master File and Local File obligations in line with BEPS Action 13, when the Luxembourg entity is the ultimate parent or a constituent entity of such a group.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg applies the OECD-integrated economic substance doctrine through several statutory layers. For a SARL engaged in freeze-dried pet food manufacturing, the company must demonstrate real, locally embedded substance: an office or production facility, employees with decision-making authority, board meetings held in Luxembourg, and operational risk management. The Luxembourg register of beneficial owners (RBE) imposes a transparency obligation; failure to file or maintain RBE data is a criminal offence. The anti-abuse provisions (GAAR under Article 6 of the Luxembourg tax code and the 2019 Law on tax abuse), together with ATAD interest restriction rules, deny tax advantages for artificial arrangements lacking commercial substance. In cross-border payment scenarios, the 2023 Luxembourg Administrative Circular concerning the beneficial ownership requirement for DTA application and the EU's 'DAC 6' mandatory disclosure rules for potentially aggressive cross-border arrangements further enforce substance. The Luxembourg common law company (société commerciale) status is never sufficient alone; the manufacturing scope with freeze-drying equipment, local warehouse, veterinary food compliance approvals, product liability insurance, and payroll in Luxembourg constitute the required economic substance. A shell company with no production activity but generating royalty or service fee income would fail the substance doctrine and be subject to requalification, denial of treaty benefits, and deemed dividend treatment.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate falsification of the corporate income tax return, suppression of freeze-dried pet food sales revenue, use of undisclosed foreign bank accounts, fabricated deductible expenses, or illicit re-invoicing through shell suppliers in another jurisdiction.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under Articles 242 to 244 of the Luxembourg Income Tax Law, fraudulent tax evasion is punishable by a fine of up to EUR 25,000, which may be multiplied per taxable year of the offence. The tax administration may additionally impose an administrative penalty of 10% of the evaded tax plus a 50% surcharge for wilful tax evasion (indices sérieux d'intention). Prosecution occurs before the Luxembourg criminal courts (tribunal correctionnel) and can lead to confiscation of goods and closure of business premises.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and the duly appointed manager (gérant) of the SARL face joint personal liability for intentionally or negligently committed unlawful acts. In tax evasion, criminal liability extends directly to the natural-person manager: imprisonment of 8 days to 5 years under Article 244 LIR possibly combined with fines. The corporate veil is pierced where the SARL is used as a mere facade or where the manager personally assisted or procured the evasion. For unpaid corporate tax liabilities resulting from fraud, the tax authority may issue a director liability notice against the gérant holding him civilly liable for the company's unpaid taxes, interest, and penalties. Additionally, the Luxembourg Criminal Code sanctions abuse of company assets and fictitious dividend distributions, enabling creditors and tax authorities to claim civil restitution from directors.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Lack of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: A Luxembourg SARL in the freeze-dried pet meat manufacturing sector that files tax returns but has no physical production facility, no employees, no locally managed bank account, and conducts all operations through a foreign sub-contractor, or uses artificial intragroup agreements to divert taxable profit without local substance.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Luxembourg GAAR (Article 6 LIR) and the 2022 Council Directive (EU) 2016/1164 implementation, any artificial arrangement or series of arrangements put in place for the essential purpose of obtaining a tax advantage is disregarded and recharacterized. The tax administration will reallocate profits to where the substance is located, impose an upward adjustment, and apply an interest charge of 0.6% per month plus a possible intentional-neglactence penalty of 10% to 50%. Additionally, non-cooperative intermediary and user arrangements require disclosure under DAC 6, with fines up to EUR 250,000 for non-disclosure.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who manage the shell company as a conduit face liability under Luxembourg civil law for misrepresenting corporate substance when applying for VAT, bank accounts, or export licences. Directors may be sued for fraudulent misrepresentation by investors or trade creditors and ordered to pay restitution out of personal assets. In the context of abuses of the domestic dividend withholding exemption or the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, the Luxembourg tax administration can — under the 'look-through' anti-abuse doctrine — treat the SARL as transparent and attribute profits directly to the ultimate non-resident shareholders. The gérant may face a travel ban to Luxembourg if judicial ex parte freezing orders are issued, though imprisonment arises only for criminal fraude fiscale.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to identify and file the ultimate natural-person beneficial owners of the SARL in the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners within one month of incorporation or any change; providing false beneficial ownership information; or continuing to receive unsettled cryptocurrency or undisclosed founder capital without source verification.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the Luxembourg Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the RBE register, non-compliance is a criminal offence: fines from EUR 1,250 to EUR 1,250,000 plus imprisonment of 6 months to 5 years for the SARL and its directors, and the possibility of publication of the administrative decision. Non-compliance also triggers a blocking of dividends and further legal acts, because financial institutions must refuse to execute corporate transactions until the RBE registration is compliant.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant and each director who knowingly participates in an AML breach face joint and several liability under the Luxembourg AML Law of 12 November 2004 (as amended) for civil damages caused to third parties. The CSSF and Luxembourg police Judiciaire can levy personal fines, impose a prohibition against managing a Luxembourg entity, and for severe breaches involving predicate crimes (e.g. laundering of funds from prohibited meat-import smuggling), arrest and imprisonment of the responsible directors. A travel ban from the Schengen area can be issued as part of coercive criminal procedure.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failure to prepare and file Annex 740 for intragroup transactions exceeding EUR 250,000 or failure to maintain an OECD-compliant transfer pricing operational file, including sale of freeze-dried pet products to a related distributor at artificially depressed prices or procurement of raw meat from a related supplier at inflated prices to shift taxable profits outside Luxembourg.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Where documentation is absent or false, the Luxembourg tax administration applies the best-method judgment and makes a transfer pricing adjustment. The adjustment is subject to an interest charge on the additional tax assessed. A specific administrative penalty of up to 25% of the tax deficiency may be imposed for failure to cooperate in the audit. In cases where transfer pricing mispricing conceals a distribution of profit to shareholders, the excess may be recharacterized as a constructive dividend subject to 15% withholding tax and administrative penalties.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The gérant who signs the tax return containing knowingly false transfer pricing documentation may be treated as having concluded an unlawful taxable agreement with the treasury. Directors can be held civilly liable under Article 110-1 of the Luxembourg Law on commercial companies for the company's audit and tax adjustments if the tax deficiency results from a serious personal fault (faute grave). If the transfer pricing scheme is used to evade corporate income tax intentionally, the criminal fraude fiscale regime with imprisonment provisions applies to the individual director who directed the scheme.
